title: Kaplow – tactical multiplayer shooter, runs in the browser
author: Drx26
selftext:

comments.body: u/Drx26 please update this post with more on how you used AI to build the game. Rule 4 is there so promotional posts add to the sub by talking about the process and real development. We don't want the sub drowned in empty promotion. Posts that aren't updated may be removed.

comments.author: Drx26
comments.body:
Edit: how it was built (per Rule 4)

Quick rundown since the mod asked. Pretty much all of the code was written with Claude Code. I did the design, testing and the “no, that feels wrong” part.

* Workflow: I ran several Claude Code sessions in parallel, each on one feature (maps, weapons, audio, bots, UI). I’d describe what I want, it builds it on a staging copy, I play it, give feedback, repeat. Nothing went live without me testing it first.
* Stack: plain JS + Three.js in the browser, Node server on a small VPS. No engine, everything procedural, so the AI could actually reason about all of it.
* What worked well: gameplay systems (Rush mode, respawn/spectator, bot loadouts, rank system), map layouts, server setup/hardening, procedural sound design.
* What was painful: first-person hands and weapon grips. Took a lot of iterations, checking screenshots at full res and changing one thing at a time. Still a bit of finger clipping on some guns.
* Assets: weapons and maps are generated in code. The arm rig is based on a CC0 skeleton, restyled. Radio voice lines are TTS.

Biggest lesson: the AI is fast, but it drifts into side quests if you let it. Keeping tasks small and checking every change yourself is what made it work.
